summary:
Prince Edward Island stands under the national framework of Canada. The province's own rules govern gender-marker changes on provincial documents, driver's licence markers, and family law.

Prince Edward Island amended its Vital Statistics Act in 2016 so that a person can change the gender on provincial official documents by declaring the gender they identify with and providing a letter from a doctor. Sex-reassignment surgery is no longer required, and the province's gender-marker change has operated without a surgery requirement since that amendment.

The change of gender designation is not open to visitors. An adult applicant must have been born in Prince Edward Island and have lived in the province for at least three months, and must not be in the lawful custody of another person. A legal custodian may apply for a minor under 18 who was born on the island and has lived there at least three months, with the written consent of any other custodian or parent and of the child if the child is 12 or older.

Since 4 December 2018, provincial driver's licences can carry 'gender not listed' (shown as X) or 'prefer not to say' (shown as blank) alongside male and female, available at Access PEI locations.

The national police-reported hate-crime release for 2024 carries no Prince Edward Island-specific rate or incident count, and no provincially deviating pattern is documented for the province.

Prince Edward Island allowed joint adoption in 2009, extending the right to couples whose relationship is classed as same-sex under provincial law.
tangentialFactors:
When the 2016 amendment was tabled by the MacLauchlan government, Pride P.E.I. board member Jesse Macmillan welcomed the removal of the surgery requirement, noting that surgery is expensive and that the nearest provider was in Montreal, and called for a third gender category, saying many of his friends in Charlottetown identify outside the binary.

The province described itself as the first jurisdiction in Canada to offer the 'prefer not to say' blank option on a driver's licence when the change took effect.
localsOnly:
An application to change gender designation requires completed forms including a physician statement, a written statement by the applicant, and a signature arranged before a commissioner of oaths at Vital Statistics.

Health PEI would cover the costs of three surgeries for transgender patients, according to a linked item on the 2016 CBC report.
outOfScopeNotes:
The current status of Health PEI's coverage of gender-affirming surgeries is not sourced beyond the 2016 linked item.

Whether provincial birth certificates offer a marker beyond male and female is not sourced; the 2018 change covered driver's licences, and the 2016 call for a third category is not documented as implemented on the birth register.

The gender-designation information page was captured on 1 July 2022, so the application requirements may have changed since.

National hate-crime analyses, including the Egale Canada analysis of police-reported data, do not disaggregate to Prince Edward Island.
